questions.stem: A user reports their Windows PC is slow at boot. After login, several applications open by themselves. Which Task Manager tab is BEST for narrowing down the cause?
questions.explanation: The Startup tab lists applications configured to launch at login. You can disable them individually to isolate the slow one.
questions.trap: Processes shows what is currently running but doesn't tell you what is configured to auto-start. Performance shows resource usage, not startup config.

questions.stem: An administrator needs to view Windows logs filtered for security-related failures. Which utility (and .msc filename) opens directly to those logs?
questions.explanation: Event Viewer (eventvwr.msc) shows Windows logs grouped into Application, Security, Setup, and System. You can filter to specific levels and sources.
questions.trap: msinfo32 is read-only system info, not logs.

questions.stem: A user complains their solid-state drive performance is degraded. A tech opens Disk Defragmenter and clicks Optimize. What is the issue?

choices.text: Defragmenting an SSD has no performance benefit and may wear the drive
Defragmentation requires Pro or higher Windows
Defragmentation requires the user to be logged off
Defragmentation cannot run on partitions smaller than 100 GB

questions.explanation: SSDs do not benefit from defragmentation - access time is uniform across cells. Repeated writes from a defrag actually reduce SSD lifespan.
questions.trap: It is technically possible to run defrag on an SSD; the issue is that it is the wrong tool. Use disk cleanup, check for malware, or check storage health instead.

questions.stem: Before changing a registry value to fix an application issue, what should the technician do FIRST?

choices.text: Export the affected registry hive to a .reg file

questions.explanation: Exporting the hive (File > Export in regedit) gives you a known-good backup you can re-import if the change breaks something.
questions.trap: Disabling Defender or running sfc do not protect against a bad registry edit. The fastest recovery path is a registry export taken before editing.

questions.stem: A technician wants to launch the Local Group Policy Editor on a single Windows 11 Pro workstation that is NOT joined to a domain. Which command should they run?
questions.explanation: gpedit.msc is the Local Group Policy Editor, used for single-machine policy. gpmc.msc is for Active Directory environments and requires RSAT.
questions.trap: lusrmgr.msc manages users / groups, not policies.

questions.stem: A tech needs to add a recurring nightly job that runs a backup script at 2 AM. Which Windows utility manages this?
questions.explanation: Task Scheduler (taskschd.msc) runs apps and scripts on triggers including daily times. Configure Triggers, Actions, Conditions, and Settings.
questions.trap: Performance Monitor collects metrics but does not schedule jobs.

questions.stem: A help desk tech sits down at an unfamiliar machine and wants ONE screen that summarizes the OS name, processor, BIOS, boot device, and installed RAM. Which utility?
questions.explanation: System Information (msinfo32.exe) System Summary gives this exact overview in one screen.
questions.trap: Resource Monitor is real-time stats, not system inventory.

questions.stem: Match each Windows tool to its primary purpose.
questions.explanation: These five tools are the most commonly tested in 1.4. Memorize the filename + purpose for each.

questions.stem: Which statements about the Windows Registry are TRUE? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The top-level keys all start with HKEY
Changes take effect immediately and may require a reboot to fully apply
The registry can be edited safely by any standard user without UAC prompts
Hives can be exported as .reg files for backup

questions.explanation: HKEYs (a), changes apply with possible reboot (b), and hives can be exported (d). regedit always prompts UAC because edits can break the OS.
questions.trap: (c) is false - UAC always prompts for regedit because of the destructive potential.
